title: Names recurring across MPAP 4 dossiers
understood: I read 'dossiers' as the family files in MPAP 4 (the groups of pages named in Laura's TEI file names), and 'similar names' as the same person or a similar spelling tagged on more than one page. Conti has no dossier field, so these steps list the tagged people with the pages they appear on, so the names can be compared across dossiers. Notaries are left out by hand (occupation 'notaio' or the title 'ser' with a notarial role).
limits: Only 10 of the 47 transcribed MPAP 4 pages have person tags, and Laura has approved none of them. A name that appears only on an untagged page will not show up in steps 1–2. Steps 4–5 search the text on all transcribed pages, but only for two sample names. Conti does not know which pages make up a dossier: the page list in step 2 has to be read against the family names in the TEI file names. Conti does not match similar spellings automatically (e.g. Francescho/Francecho, Vanni/Nanni di Chastello): it compares tagged names as written. Telling namesakes from the same person needs a reading of the entries.

bardi.title: Check across all transcribed pages: where the Bardi are written

caveats: MPAP_4: only 10 of 47 included pages are tagged (593 pages in the manuscript), so people and occupations are partial.

answer.headline: Not on present evidence: the two names checked across all 47 pages, Miniato and the Bardi, each stay within one dossier. Only one Bardi-dossier page is tagged, so the full comparison remains untested.
answer.answer:
The data can't yet support a full cross-dossier comparison. Person tags exist on only 10 of the 47 included MPAP 4 pages (239 person tags). Nine of those pages belong to the Deo di Vanni pages (RS1108–RS1128). Only one, RS1138 (headed "REDE DI DOFFO DI GIOVANNI DE BARDI"), comes from the Bardi pages [people_pages]. So the tagged names mostly cover a single dossier, and no plan step listed which pages each tagged person appears on.

I searched the text of every included page, tagged or not, for the two strongest candidates. The most frequent tagged name, Miniato di messer Arrigo (55 tags; he is the heirs' attore), is written in 94 lines on 18 pages. All of them fall between RS1108 and RS1134, and none is on RS1138 or later [miniato]. The search also caught variant spellings ("minato", "niniato", "me ato"). It also included "miniato mazziere", a tenant on RS1110 l9, who may be a different man. In the other direction, "Bardi" occurs in 15 lines on 8 pages, all between RS1138 and RS1147, and on none of the Deo di Vanni pages [bardi]. So neither name links the two dossiers.

Within the Bardi pages, names do recur from page to page. Bindo di messer Iacopo de' Bardi and a Ruberto de' Bardi are named on RS1138 (as substitute heirs and tutors) and again as a neighbour (confine) on RS1140 l4, and "Ruberto de bardi" holds land on RS1142 [bardi]. Those pages may themselves be more than one dossier: RS1143 is headed "Rede del calonaco debardi", and RS1139 and RS1145 both refer to an act of 16 May 1388 [bardi]. If so, these Bardi names are the clearest case of the same people across dossiers, but within one family.

On notaries: the [notaries] step doesn't isolate them. It returns every person in any entry that mentions a notary, 36 lines in all. That set mixes notaries (ser Jacopo di Vanuccio, ser Giovanni Lappi and Barone di Simone on RS1126; ser Nigi di ser Giovanni on RS1138) with heirs, widows and officials such as the camarlingo Antonio di Davanzato. None of those names is shown on both sides.

caveats: Dossier boundaries are not recorded in Conti. They are inferred here from page headings (RS1138 "Rede di Doffo…", RS1143 "Rede del calonaco…") and from page ranges, so 'one dossier to another' rests on that inference.
Only two names were searched across all pages. Every other tagged name (e.g. Francescho Marchi, Cola di Guglielmo, the Davizi) was not tested against the other dossier.

The text search is approximate. It matched spelling variants of Miniato and may include a different Miniato (the mazziere on RS1110). Ruberto is 'di Bindo' in the tag but 'di dosso' (probably 'doffo') on RS1140, so these may be two Robertos.
None of the 459 tags has been approved yet. All are Claude suggestions.
